Define partial sums $P_0 = 0$, $P_m = \sum_{j=1}^m d_j$ for $m = 1, \ldots, 19$. Then $a_k = a_1 + P_{k-1}$.

## Reducing to the Range of Partial Sums

Since the $d_j$ are strictly increasing, $P_m$ is a **convex sequence** (second differences $P_{m+1} - 2P_m + P_{m-1} = d_{m+1} - d_m \geq 1$). A convex sequence attains its maximum at an endpoint, so:

$$\max_k a_k = a_1 + \max(P_0, P_{19})$$

The minimum of $a_k$ is $a_1 + \min_m P_m$, and we need all $a_k \geq 1$, so $a_1 \geq 1 - \min_m P_m$.

Setting $a_1$ to its minimum value $1 - \min_m P_m$:

$$\max_k a_k = 1 - \min_m P_m + \max(P_0, P_{19}) = 1 + \max_m P_m - \min_m P_m = 1 + \text{Range}(P)$$

So **minimizing the maximum security level equals minimizing the range of the partial sums $P_0, \ldots, P_{19}$**.

## Lower Bound on the Range

$$P_0 - P_{m^*} = \sum_{j=1}^{m^*}(-d_j) \geq \sum_{j=1}^{m^*}(m^* - j) = \frac{m^*(m^*-1)}{2}$$

**Right sum** (rise from $P_{m^*}$ to $P_{19}$): Since $d_j \geq d_{m^*+1} + (j - m^* - 1) \geq j - m^* - 1$:

$$P_{19} - P_{m^*} = \sum_{j=m^*+1}^{19} d_j \geq \sum_{j=m^*+1}^{19}(j - m^* - 1) = \frac{(19-m^*)(18-m^*)}{2}$$

The range is $\max(P_0 - P_{m^*},\; P_{19} - P_{m^*})$, so:

$$\text{Range} \geq \max\!\left(\frac{m^*(m^*-1)}{2},\;\frac{(19-m^*)(18-m^*)}{2}\right)$$

For all other $m^*$, the value is strictly larger. Therefore:

$$\text{Range} \geq 45$$
